# The split deleted 12 src/ai unit specs whose subjects still ship

## Context

`c623b2f63c` (`feat(engine): remove received Brain implementation (#17791) (#17806)`) deleted 796 unit specs under one general account. #17922 hand-censused a slice of that population — `test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/**` — and explicitly scoped the other 774 deletions out, noting that *"a general 'does this deleted spec's subject still exist in the Engine?' sweep is worth doing and is not this."*

That general sweep now exists as a mechanical instrument: the surviving-subject check built in #17964 / PR #17965. Replaying it over `c623b2f63c` surfaced a population nothing had censused — **12 deleted specs whose subjects are still in `src/ai/**` at `HEAD` today, and whose arms no CI anywhere executes.**

This ticket is the durable owner that RA-4 of @neo-gpt's review on PR #17965 required. It was recorded in #17964's *Out of Scope* precisely so it could not be quietly absorbed, and it is filed rather than left as prose.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-31T18:27Z; no equivalent found. Nearest neighbours are #17922 (a different, already-censused slice) and #17967 (skill *references* to `ai/` paths, not test coverage).

## The Problem

A deleted spec is the one regression the suite cannot report: the run goes green with less coverage behind the same number. For these 12 the implementation never left — only its tests did — so nothing anywhere is red, nothing is missing at import time, and the loss is invisible to every existing signal.

Verified at `HEAD`, all twelve subjects present, none carrying an Engine spec:

| Subject (still shipping) | Spec deleted in `c623b2f63c` |
|---|---|
| `src/ai/LockRegistry.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/LockRegistry.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/TransactionService.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/TransactionService.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/WriteGuard.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/WriteGuard.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/admitWrite.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/admitWrite.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/deriveSubtreePath.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/deriveSubtreePath.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/parseAgentEnvelope.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/parseAgentEnvelope.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/resolveWriteLock.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/resolveWriteLock.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/client/ComponentService.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/client/ComponentService.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/client/DockService.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/client/DockService.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/client/InstanceService.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/client/InstanceService.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/client/RuntimeService.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/client/RuntimeService.spec.mjs` |
| `src/ai/client/TourRunner.mjs` | `test/playwright/unit/ai/client/TourRunner.spec.mjs` |

Measured, not inferred: each subject path exists at `HEAD` and `find test/playwright/unit -name '<name>.spec.mjs'` returns nothing for all twelve. The deleted paths are read from `c623b2f63c`'s own `--name-status` rows.

That census is **Engine-scoped**, and the scope is the correction below: it cannot see a spec that moved to another repository, so its silence was read as absence.

Note what this population is NOT. The engine kept these files deliberately — they are the Engine-side write-admission and client-service surface, not Brain implementation that departed. The split correctly removed a great deal; it also took the tests of things it kept.

## Correction — the original premise was false, and so was its first repair

This ticket shipped with *"no unit coverage at all"*. @neo-gpt's review on PR #18002 falsified it: all twelve specs are tracked on `neo-agent-brain` `origin/dev@a212acc` at byte-identical paths, importing the Engine as a package (`neo.mjs/src/ai/...`). `c623b2f63c` **moved** this coverage; it did not delete it.

The first repair — mine, in A2A — then overshot in the other direction: I ran the Brain specs locally, saw them pass, and reported that they *"are selected and they run."* Selected is true; run is not. `.github/workflows/brain-unit.yml` collects the whole corpus with `npm run test-unit -- --list`, then executes an explicit four-file smoke list:

    test/playwright/unit/ai/AgentOrchestrator.spec.mjs
    test/playwright/unit/ai/Env.spec.mjs
    test/playwright/unit/harness/terminateDaemon.spec.mjs
    test/playwright/unit/ai/daemons/orchestrator/scheduling/pipeline.spec.mjs

None of the twelve is in it. Engine's `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `npm run test-${{ matrix.suite }}` with no file list, so the Engine `unit` suite executes its full corpus.

This collected-but-never-executed property is **not a new finding** — `neo-agent-brain#201` already owns it, and states it more precisely than I did (*"healthy retained specs never selected — collected successfully, assertions never run"*). It is cited here only to explain why the original census read absence into a repository whose CI would not have reported these arms either way.

**Current truth, three-valued rather than two:** the twelve arms *exist* (Brain), are *collected* (Brain `--list`, so an import or syntax break is still caught), and are *executed by nothing*. The defect this ticket describes is therefore real and slightly sharper than filed — the write-admission refusal path has arms that no pipeline ever runs — but its stated mechanism was wrong, and the fix is custody, not authorship: restoring these subjects' specs to the Engine is what puts them in a suite that actually executes them.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The write-admission chain is the sharp half.** `admitWrite` / `WriteGuard` / `resolveWriteLock` / `LockRegistry` / `TransactionService` form a refusal path — the class of code whose failure mode is *permitting* something, which is exactly the failure a passing suite cannot notice. Coverage loss here is worth more than the count suggests.
- **`src/ai/client/**` is the consumed surface** the Neural Link drives; `deriveSubtreePath` and `parseAgentEnvelope` are pure functions and are the cheapest arms to restore.
- **The specs are recoverable, not rewritable-from-scratch:** `git show c623b2f63c^:<path>` yields each original. They will not apply unmodified — they were written against the pre-split module graph — so restoration is a port, and the ported arm must be checked against what the subject does *now*.
- **`test/playwright/unit` is the only Engine suite CI runs** alongside `components`, so restored specs land where they will actually execute.

## The Fix

Port each deleted spec back against its current subject, under its original path. Per subject: recover the original, run it, and repair it against today's API — the arm must fail when the subject misbehaves, not merely pass.

Restoration is not the moment to change what an implementation does. If a ported arm reveals a defect in the subject, that is a separate bug ticket, and this ticket records it rather than fixing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 12 subjects carry a unit spec at its original path under `test/playwright/unit/ai/**`, and `npm run test-unit` is green.
- [ ] Each restored spec is mutation-checked: a seeded change to its subject reds at least one arm. A spec that cannot fail on its subject's defect does not count as restored, and the seeded mutation is stated per subject.
- [ ] The write-admission chain (`admitWrite`, `WriteGuard`, `resolveWriteLock`, `LockRegistry`, `TransactionService`) has at least one arm per subject asserting a REFUSAL, not only a success path.
- [ ] Any port that had to change an assertion because the subject's behavior changed since `c623b2f63c` names the change and why the new assertion is correct.
- [ ] The twelve arms are **executed by Engine CI**, not merely present: the `unit` suite's own run at the merge head reports each restored spec file in its collected-and-executed set, and the count is recorded as `passed / skipped` rather than as a collected total.
- [ ] The Brain copies are retired in a paired, Engine-first sequence, so the twelve exist in exactly one repository when both PRs have landed. (The #17964 surviving-subject guard evaluates the *deleting* commit and structurally cannot observe a later restoration, so it is not the instrument for this AC; that limitation is recorded in #17964 rather than worked around here.)
- [ ] Defects found while porting are filed as their own tickets and linked here; none are fixed in this PR.

## Out of Scope

- **The other 762 deletions.** #17922 censused one slice, this ticket censuses a second; neither claims the remainder. Most covered `ai/**` sources that genuinely left with the split.
- **Changing any of the 12 implementations.** Restoration is not a refactor, and a defect surfaced by a port becomes its own ticket.
- **The five subjects whose filename differs from their spec's** (`TicketIndex.spec.mjs` → `tickets.mjs`, and similar) — no mechanical name rule recovers those; they belong to #17922's stated bound.
- **Making the spec-retirement guard blocking** — #17171 owns required-context binding for the `*-lint.yml` workflows.

## Avoided Traps

- **Restoring the files unmodified and calling it done.** The specs predate the split's module graph; a green run after a blind restore would most likely mean the arms are vacuous, which is why the mutation criterion above is per-spec rather than per-PR.
- **Treating the count as the goal.** Twelve specs is the population, not the value; the write-admission chain is where the coverage actually matters, and it is called out separately so a port that runs out of budget stops at the right place.
- **Folding this into #17922.** That ticket's instrument and stated bound are a different population. Bundling would silently widen a claim it deliberately narrowed.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — restores test coverage for existing behavior; no contract, no ADR authority touched.

## Progress — AC-1 met, AC-3 met behaviourally, AC-2 at 7/12

All 12 specs restored at their original paths. **Full unit suite: 2882 passed, 0 failed, 0 did not run** (AC-1).

### AC-2 mutation ledger — 7 of 12

Each mutation was applied to the **subject**, run, and reverted to a clean tree. A subject is counted only when a seeded change reds at least one arm.

| Subject | Seeded mutation | Arms red |
|---|---|---|
| `deriveSubtreePath` | `path.unshift` → `path.push` (ancestor order reversed) | 3 of 6 |
| `parseAgentEnvelope` | `agentId.length > 0` → `>= 0` (empty id passes instead of failing closed to `null`) | 1 |
| `admitWrite` | `!writeGuard` branch `admitted:false` → `true` (fail-closed → fail-open) | 1 |
| `resolveWriteLock` | `agentId.length > 0` → `>= 0` (half-stamped writer pair no longer denied) | 2 |
| `WriteGuard` | invalid lease clock/ttl `granted:false` → `true` | 1 |
| `LockRegistry` | `if (conflict)` → `if (false && conflict)` (cross-writer overlap stops denying) | 1 |
| `TransactionService` | `no-open-transaction` `{ok:false}` → `{ok:true}` | 2 |

Remaining: `ComponentService`, `DockService`, `InstanceService`, `RuntimeService`, `TourRunner`.

### AC-3 — the write-admission chain, met behaviourally rather than by keyword

A keyword census finds refusal language in all five (`admitWrite` 13 arms, `WriteGuard` 25, `resolveWriteLock` 8, `LockRegistry` 36, `TransactionService` 26) — but token presence is not proof that a refusal is *asserted*. So each of the five was mutated to make its guard **permissive**, and each reds. A spec that only exercised success paths would have stayed green under every one of those seven mutations. That is the AC's intent discharged with evidence rather than with a grep.

### Observation, deliberately not a new ticket

`Document.computeShapeFingerprint` accepts a document whose `zones` carry a bare-string descriptor, while `getZoneNodeId` resolves only the record form — so such a document **passes the shape gate and indexes to nothing**: `TopologyDiff` reports zero moves and zero errors on it. That is what made the ported `diffDockTopology` arm fail in a way that pointed two layers below the cause.

Recording it here rather than filing: it belongs to the model's validation surface, not to this restoration, and per the fold-before-file discipline an observation on an owning ticket beats a new orphan. Worth a leaf if anyone touches that gate.

Still open: AC-2 for the remaining 5, and AC-5's replay of the `#17964` surviving-subject guard.
